statement: For every independent product input with one-dimensional densities bounded by one and every real symmetric A with rank(A)>=3, the law of X^TAX has an individually bounded density in C0(R). A selected invertible physical principal block of order 3 or 4 yields a finite but matrix-dependent height C_d/sigma_min(B).
new_tail_lemma: For an invertible d=3 or4 physical block, the output measure contributed by |x|>=R has interval-density constant at most d^(3/2)/(sigma_min(B) R), implying an explicit O(|t-c0|^(-1/2)) density tail after completing the square.
remaining_gap: No dimension- and matrix-independent upper bound on the attained pointwise maxima is proved.
